archive_file_inventory.classification_method: Every hash-manifest entry is classified using archive reason, filename, path, recovered linkedFrom context, and captured HTML synopsis when present. Assessment status is source-qualified. Clinical/topic assertions require objective/assessment evidence; the presence of a linked file, lab listing, practice quiz or literal word is not treated as proof of final-paper coverage.

confirmed_assessment_model.confirmed: Guide objectives state expected section knowledge; listed Drugs to Know are expected by course end and may be asked in assignments and exam; section revision questions are described as excellent final-exam study tools.
confirmed_assessment_model.source_quote: These objectives are there to guide you in your study as they outline the knowledge you are expected to gain by the end of the section and of what we expect you to know. Also included at the beginning of most sections is a “Drugs to Know” list. These are lists of specific drugs that are in common use and of which we expect you to know. You will be expected to be familiar with these drugs by the end of the course and may be asked about them in assignments and in the exam.

confirmed_assessment_model.confirmed: No separate drug-calculation test; basic/simple calculations and checking dose safety matter, with examples of types that could be asked.
confirmed_assessment_model.source_quote: This course no longer includes a drugs calculation section and there is no longer a drug calculations test. However, as this paper is covering the basic principles of Pharmacology it is important that you can do simple dose calculations and be able to tell if a dose is safe. If you are a Nursing student, you will have covered drug calculations in your other courses. For students who are not Nursing students or those who want to see examples of the types of calculations which you could be asked, see appendix 1.

integrated_care_exam_preparation_model.preparation_logic: The supplied test guidance confirms MCQ, true/false and short-answer formats but does not say how often any topic or task family appears. Ordinary cards build one fact or decision at a time; linked supports make the prerequisites learnable; full references preserve multi-part reasoning. The five interaction exemplars add repeated practice in choosing, judging, interpreting a visual, or composing an answer. These are preparation pathways, not evidence that a particular exam question will recur or that a learner will pass.
